title: Thermodynamics of Membrane Protein Folding Measured by Fluorescence Spectroscopy
protocol: Aliquot 20 mg of DMPC lipids in chloroform into clean glass vials.
Add a layer of nitrogen gas to each vial to prevent lipid oxidation.
Seal the vials with caps and parafilm.
Store the vials at -20°C until use.
Retrieve a single vial containing 20 mg lipid in chloroform for each experiment.
Dry the contents of the vial using a stream of nitrogen gas for 1 hour.
Resuspend dried lipids in 1 mL of 20 mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH = 7.3) using a water bath sonicator for ~30 seconds.
Transfer the cloudy solution to a plastic 15-mL tube with a conical bottom.
Add another 1 mL aliquot of phosphate buffer to the empty glass vial that originally contained lipid, and repeat sonication; transfer this solution to the same 15-mL tube.
Repeat the process three more times until the final volume in the tube is 4 mL, resulting in a lipid concentration of 5 mg/mL in the stock vesicle solution.
Place the 4 mL volume of lipid vesicle solution in a warm (~30°C) water bath and sonicate using an ultrasonicator microtip for 1 hour at 50% duty cycle.
Pass the sonicated solution through a 0.22 μm syringe filter to remove debris from the sonicator tip.
Equilibrate the filtered solution overnight at 37°C.
Make a stock solution of 10 M urea in 20 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.3).
Add solutes to a clean, empty bottle and add water up to the intended final volume for the urea solution.
Warm the urea solution in a water bath or on a hot plate with stirring to dissolve the solute if necessary.
Determine the actual concentration of the urea stock solution using refractive index.
Make a stock buffer solution of 20 mM phosphate (pH 7.3).
Prepare a stock protein solution with a concentration of ~200 μM in 8 M urea, 20 mM phosphate buffer.

Combine appropriate volumes of stock protein, stock lipid solution, stock 10 M urea solution, and stock phosphate buffer to make samples containing ~4 μM protein, 1 mg/mL lipid, and 0 to 8 M urea in 1 M increments.
Ensure the total volume of each sample is 200 μL.
Make blank samples as described, but without adding protein.
Add 4 μL of an 8 M urea solution in place of protein to match concentrations of other components.
Incubate all samples and blanks at 37°C for at least 2 hours before measurement.
Measure tryptophan fluorescence of each sample using a steady-state fluorometer.
Record fluorescence spectra with excitation wavelength of 290 nm from 305 to 500 nm.
Utilize a microvolume fused silica cuvette with 160 μL capacity for measurements.
Maintain sample temperature at 30°C during measurement.
Load fluorescence spectra into software such as Igor Pro, Matlab, Origin, or Excel.
Subtract signal from the urea and lipid vesicle background using the following procedure.
Obtain Spectrum A by measuring the raw fluorescence spectrum of the protein in the presence of lipid vesicles and a specific concentration of urea.
Measure Spectrum B as the raw fluorescence spectrum of a corresponding blank sample containing lipid vesicles and the same urea concentration; ensure no protein is present in the blank samples.
Measure blank spectra every ~0.5 M step in urea concentration range.
Prepare additional samples in urea concentrations between 2 and 4 M in 0.2 M increments for precise measurement of free energy of unfolding.
